tier_rationale: Bambu Lab operates a real vendor cloud (Bambu Handy app, MakerWorld, cloud slicing/print queue) and the A1 ships Wi-Fi-connected by default, but Bambu's own wiki documents that account login is a separate, skippable step from Wi-Fi setup, and states plainly for this model: 'When the printer is not networked, you can export files to the SD card and initiate print jobs from there' -- i.e. core printing works with the printer never touching Bambu's servers and no account of any kind.
the_unplug_test: Block the router or never connect the A1 to a network at all, and it still prints: slice the model in Bambu Studio on your own computer (a local, free application; no login is needed to slice or export), copy the resulting file to the printer's micro SD card, and start the print from the touchscreen. Bambu's own documentation describes this SD-card path explicitly for an unnetworked printer. What you lose offline is remote monitoring and control through the Bambu Handy app, cloud print notifications, MakerWorld's cloud slicing, and multi-printer fleet management -- all of it optional layered on top of a printer that prints the same way with or without it. A January 2025 firmware change briefly threatened to gate more of this behind cloud authentication and caused a public dispute with the third-party slicer community; Bambu's current wiki documents a 'Developer Mode' that, together with LAN Only mode, still opens the printer's local MQTT/FTP channel for full third-party control with no cloud account, which is what this record is based on.
offline_losses: Bambu Handy app remote monitoring and control
AI-model-based spaghetti/failure detection updates (falls back to the last on-device model)

repairability.notes: Bambu Lab's own wiki publishes a full maintenance section for the A1 with individual replacement guides for the mainboard, AC board, heatbed, belts, motors and touchscreen, and sells the parts directly.

sources.supports: Bambu Lab's own A1-specific manual: 'When the printer is not networked, you can export files to the SD card and initiate print jobs from there,' with a full walkthrough of slicing in Bambu Studio and printing from the A1's Micro SD card slot with no network or cloud step involved.

Documents that enabling LAN Only mode plus Developer Mode 'will open the MQTT channel, live stream, and FTP, giving you full control over your printer' for third-party software, entirely on the local network, and is available on all current printer series including the A series.

Shows that connecting to Wi-Fi and logging in to a Bambu account are two distinct, sequential steps in the printer's own settings menu -- account binding ('Login') is described as a separate action taken after network setup, not a precondition of it.

Bambu's security documentation states 'LAN mode can also be used on Bambu Lab printers to allow the printer to function without the need for Cloud communication,' with control handled by a local MQTT broker running inside the printer itself.

General SD-card FAQ, applicable across the printer line including A1: printing via Micro SD card 'bypasses the cloud server' entirely and generates no cloud notification, confirming SD-card printing is a fully local code path rather than a cloud print routed back down.

open_questions: Whether the A1 includes Bluetooth Low Energy hardware (Bambu's security page attributes BLE account-binding specifically to the P1 series; the A1 uses the same ESP32 SoC family per Bambu's open-source-software page, but BLE presence on A1 specifically was not independently confirmed).

Current retail price could not be confirmed: the manufacturer's US store is a JavaScript-rendered page that did not expose price in static HTML, and third-party retailer pages (Micro Center, fccid.io) returned bot-protection challenges rather than content.

fccid.io grantee search for Bambu Lab / its Chinese legal entity returned a bot-protection challenge rather than results, so fcc_id and a sibling-grant comparison could not be established in this pass.

Whether the January 2025 authorization-control dispute (Bambu Lab announced mandatory authentication for firmware upgrades, print-job initiation and remote video, alarming the OrcaSlicer/third-party community) constitutes a ledger-worthy vendor incident is flagged to the maintainer separately; the record's own tier is based on the currently-documented state of LAN Only + Developer Mode, not on the vendor's past conduct.

Whether the standard out-of-box setup wizard presents an explicit 'skip Wi-Fi / skip account' option versus simply not enforcing one at any step was not directly observed (based on documentation review, not a hands-on unboxing).
notes: The sharper, better-sourced half of this domain's contested case. Bambu Lab's January 2025 firmware update, which threatened to require cloud authentication for functions including local print-job initiation, caused a genuine public dispute with the OrcaSlicer/third-party-slicer community (Hackaday, Tom's Hardware, All3DP, 3D Printing Industry all covered it) and is real, dated, and worth a maintainer decision on the vendor ledger. It is not treated as a tier input here per project rules. What settles the tier is Bambu's own *current* wiki documentation (accessed today, 19+ months after the dispute): SD-card printing bypasses the cloud outright and is documented per-model for the A1, and LAN Only + Developer Mode still exposes a full local MQTT/FTP control channel with no account. See bambu-lab-a1's pairing with prusa-mk4s in alternatives on any future record that rejects a Bambu model, and prusa-mk4s.json's own notes for the reverse pointer.
local_replacement_note: OrcaSlicer (open-source fork of Bambu Studio) plus LAN Only + Developer Mode reproduces slicing and printer control entirely on hardware the owner runs; Home Assistant's community Bambu Lab integration uses the same local MQTT channel to rebuild the Handy app's monitoring and notifications without any cloud account.
